STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is about 22 cm across its width (roughly a side-plate size). Area ≈ 22 x 22 ≈ 484 cm^2 for the square outline, but the plate's effective area is closer to a 20 cm round equivalent, so use ≈ 314 cm^2 as the working vessel area.

STEP 3 - Items: One piece of cooked bacon, roughly 2 long strips joined into an L-shape (a curled section near the upper left and a long strip running across the lower middle to the right).

STEP 4 - Area: Bacon covers about 12% of the plate area (≈ 38 cm^2 of the vessel), since the strip is thin and fairly narrow (about 1.5 to 2 cm wide along most of its length, total length roughly 30 cm).

STEP 5 - Volume: 38 cm^2 x 0.4 cm average thickness ≈ 15 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: 15 ml x 0.9 (dense cooked meat) ≈ 14 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked bacon ≈ 540 kcal per 100 g. 14 g x 5.4 ≈ 76 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single cooked bacon strip is typically about 8 to 12 g, and this visible piece is a long, somewhat fragmented strip of comparable size, so roughly 14 g is plausible, slightly generous. Reasonable to keep at about 14 g.

Estimated total: about 14 g, about 76 kcal.
